programmes.t: Ancient Engineering S1 - "Stone Age Secrets"
programmes.d: Even before the start of recorded history, ancient engineers across the World were erecting giant monuments. What was their purpose?

programmes.t: Ancient Engineering S1 - "The Taj Mahal And The Golden Age Of Islam"
programmes.d: Awe-inspiring palaces are the legacy that demonstrates the brilliance of Islamic engineers, culminating arguably the most beautiful building in the World - the Taj Mahal.

programmes.t: Ancient Engineering S2 - "Earliest Arenas: The Colosseum"
programmes.d: Since their earliest existence in ancient Greek and Roman civilizations, stadiums have been regarded as achitectural masterpieces and focal poins in their surrounding cities, but none more so than the Colosseum in Rome.

programmes.t: The Military Tech Show S1 - "USS Zumwalt, Tank Training, Special Forces Vehicle"
programmes.d: We reveal eye-witness intelligence on the USS Zumwalt, America's ultra-hi tech, four billion dollar guided missile destroyer. Learn more about the British firm who've developed Minerva, an ingenious, low-cost but realistic tank simulator.

programmes.t: The Military Tech Show S1 - "Typhoon Fighter, Combat Medics, USS Dwight D. Eisenhower"
programmes.d: The Military Tech Show captures the moment when BAE System's radical new pilot helmet, the Striker II, goes operational for the first time in a Typhoon fighter aircraft; how interactive technology is helping train military combat medics.

programmes.t: The Military Tech Show S1 - "Spear 3 Missile, Battlefield VR, Spy Drones"
programmes.d: European manufacturer MBDA give a hands-on demonstration of their state-of-the-art missile, the Spear 3. Learn how scientists are using a virtual reality headset to see the battlefield in a revealing new way.

programmes.t: The Military Tech Show S1 - "Radar Tech, Imperial War Museum, Land Mine Detection"
programmes.d: We have rare access to the German Aerospace Center outside Munich where scientists are using new forms of radar for surveillance and detecting land mines.

programmes.t: The Military Tech Show S1 - "RAF Station, Typhoon Squadron, The Flight Deck"
programmes.d: We're at Royal Air Force station Brize Norton, Oxfordshire, where we've been given an exclusive look at the RAF's ground-breaking, multi-role refuelling and transporter aircraft, the Voyager.

programmes.t: War Factories S1 - "German Aviation"
programmes.d: The untold secret story of war production that shaped the WWII, beginning with how the German aviation industry came to dominate the skies of Europe.

programmes.t: War Factories S1 - "Krupp"
programmes.d: The story behind the Krupp company, who were responsible for the manufacture of two of Germany's most feared war products - the Panzer Tank and the U-boat.

programmes.t: War Factories S1 - "Vickers"
programmes.d: The role played by engineering giant Vickers during the WWII, including the development of the Spitfire.

programmes.t: War Factories S1 - "General Motors"
programmes.d: How the Americans out-produced the rest of the world so quickly and by such a huge margin, including the likes of General Motors.

programmes.t: Battle Factory S1 - "An Assault Rifle, a Bomb Suit, a Mortar, and a Zodiac"
programmes.d: What starts off as a seven-pound bar of solid steel will soon deliver a bullet with deadly accuracy when it becomes the barrel of a Colt C7 assault rifle, and when plastic and bulletproof fabric are molded and stitched together,they’ll make a suit of armour made for the most dangerous job in the wor

programmes.t: Battle Factory S1 - "A Parajet, a Hovercraft, a Camo Jacket, and a Portable Military Shelter"
programmes.d: As lightweight aluminum is cut and tooled, it will become the frame of a personal flying machine. Used by military operatives, drug enforcement agents, and first responders – it gets you in and out fast, whether you are carrying a camera or a gun.

programmes.t: Battle Factory S1 - "A Sniper Rifle, a Zeppelin, a Ka-Bar Knife, and Dragon Eggs"
programmes.d: In 48 hours, a block of metal will be formed into the most accurate weapon on earth: the AX-338 Sniper Rifle. In a warzone, police stand off, or hostage taking, the sniper is often the only solution to a bad situation.

programmes.t: The Military Tech Show S1 - "Targeting & Tracking, Navigation, Seagoing Drones"
programmes.d: We reveal an experimental sensor, monitoring and targeting system developed for troops by the UK's Defence Science and Technology Laboratory and Roke Manor Research. The iXblue Marins navigation black box guides navy ships.

programmes.t: The Military Tech Show S1 - "NATO Maritime Centre, No Shipping-No Shopping"
programmes.d: We visit NATO's Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation in La Spezia, Italy. We learn how the world's oceans are one of the last places that military technology can be hidden from prying eyes.

programmes.t: Massive Moves S1 - "Historic House"
programmes.d: A family in Calgary call in a team of house truckers to move a historic colonial house to help give them – and their five children – more living space.

programmes.t: The Lightbulb Moment S1 - "LIKE BUTTON"
programmes.d: When first presented with the like button Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg had a simple response: “No.” He worried that it would discourage more meaningful online interaction. Eventually, his team changed his mind and transformed the world.

programmes.t: The Lightbulb Moment S1 - "CUBICLE"
programmes.d: A futuristic designer, Robert Propst, dreamed up “The Action Office” as a workplace utopia that would unleash the modern knowledge worker’s vast untapped potential.

programmes.t: The Lightbulb Moment S1 - "BARCODE"
programmes.d: Barcodes have radically changed global commerce, helping fuel the rise of everything from massive companies like Walmart to world powers like China. And it all started with a man daydreaming on a beach in 1949.

programmes.t: The Aviators S1 - "Day in the Life of an Airline Pilot"
programmes.d: Raeleen shows us what a typical day is like for her as an airline first officer.

programmes.t: Xploration Earth 2050 S1 - "The Future of Driving"
programmes.d: Join host Joe Penna as he discovers where this invention is headed in the run-up to 2050.

programmes.t: Oddly Satisfying Science S1 - "Explosive Elements"
programmes.d: This week's experiments include recreating a big bang with lithium, the incendiary power of methane, and how a little bit of liquified nitrogen can lend a lot of power to a rocket.

programmes.t: Oddly Satisfying Science S1 - "Colorful Conundrums"
programmes.d: This week's experiments highlight how electricity can tint titanium, how you can create a color wheel by lighting things on fire, and why the world gets all its colors from white light.

programmes.t: Oddly Satisfying Science S1 - "Don't Believe Your Eyes"
programmes.d: This week's experiments delve into the possibilities of mind control, why objects and people tend to sync together, and the magical mysteries behind magnesium.

programmes.t: Oddly Satisfying Science S1 - "The Sound of Science"
programmes.d: This week's experiments hit high notes as we discover the physics of theremins, investigate how the outer ear impacts human hearing, and put on a laser show with cymatics.

programmes.t: Bright Now S1 - "Asteroid or Alien Tech?"
programmes.d: It was discovered on October 19th, 2017 and it was recognized as the first known object of its type. It is unique since it is the first known object that came from our solar system. But while we observed it, the mystery surrounding it grew.

programmes.t: Xploration Outer Space S2 - "Space Disasters"
programmes.d: Join host Emily Calandrelli as she explores the most prominent disasters in our journey through the cosmos, and what we learned from each set-back.

programmes.t: Xploration Outer Space S2 - "Why We Explore"
programmes.d: Host Emily Calandrelli makes the case for space exploration.

programmes.t: Xploration Outer Space S2 - "Exoplanets"
programmes.d: Join host Emily Calandrelli as she explores the fascinating world of exoplanets.

programmes.t: Xploration Outer Space S2 - "Building and Testing Rockets"
programmes.d: Join Emily Calandrelli as she tours a 1 million square foot facility in Alabama that is manufacturing some of the world’s most powerful rockets.

programmes.t: Hollywood Weapons: Fact or Fiction? S1 - "Schapbo"
programmes.d: John Rambo’s ability to decimate enemies all by himself has created some of the most incredible weapon stunts in Hollywood history. We test the reality surrounding these iconic scenes from this blockbuster franchise.

programmes.t: Hollywood Weapons: Fact or Fiction? S1 - "Terry and the Minigun"
programmes.d: Can you really fire a GE Minigun handheld with ammunition held in a backpack (also seen on Captain America: Winter Soldier). Additionally, for one of our larger tests – can you actually chop down a jungle forest with a minigun?

programmes.t: Hollywood Weapons: Fact or Fiction? S1 - "Scoreless"
programmes.d: Using a unique method to crack a safe, Nick Wells (Robert De Niro) uses a blowtorch to cut through a safe, fill it with water, and blow the door off using a small explosive device.

programmes.t: Hollywood Weapons: Fact or Fiction? S1 - "Terry Vs Gorn"
programmes.d: Captain James T Kirk’s battle with the Gorn alien is one of the most popular episodes from the original series. He defeats the Gorn by creating gunpowder from the base elements found on the planet.

programmes.t: The New Frontier S2 - "Mars: Adapt or Leave"
programmes.d: As the latest successes and failures come and go Mars continues to give up her secrets. Invisible clouds are revealed with ultraviolet light and the search for the source of methane continues with ExoMars.

programmes.t: The New Frontier S2 - "Emissaries"
programmes.d: Our solar system is vast, from our own star the Sun to Earth is nearly 150 million kilometers or 1 Astronomical Unit. Jupiter is 5.2 AU distant and Pluto up to 48AU, the solar system extends far beyond this into interstellar space.

programmes.t: The New Frontier S2 - "Danger Asteroids Ahead"
programmes.d: The question often rises is the cost of space exploration really worth it? Could the money be better spent elsewhere. If so one space program would have to remain. The planetary defence program, to locate identify and deflect a wayward asteroid.

programmes.t: The New Frontier S2 - "First Light"
programmes.d: For an instrument first developed as recently as the 17th century, the telescope has travelled a long way. The latest version of the once-humble telescope will be going a lot farther – carrying us ever closer to the first light.

programmes.t: The Re-Inventors S1 - "Floatation Suit"
programmes.d: It looks like a doghouse resting on a wet suit, but this 1916 invention could have savez countless lives lost at sea.

programmes.t: The Re-Inventors S1 - "Head Parachute"
programmes.d: Personal fire escape for people trapped in buildings, that must work. Will it save your life or not? Let's see.

programmes.t: The Re-Inventors S1 - "Gun Helmet"
programmes.d: A steel helmet with an air-power-triggered gun welded to the top. What could possibly go wrong?

programmes.t: The Re-Inventors S1 - "Flying Machine"
programmes.d: Join Re-Inventors Matt and Jeremy as they take this pedal-powered ancestor to the helicopter on a test flight.

programmes.t: Around the World in 80 Tricks S1 - "Manchester"
programmes.d: Pete Heat checks out some of the trendiest bars in the Mumbai, meets a famous Bollywood artist and shows you how to perform your own piece of magic at home.

programmes.t: Around the World in 80 Tricks S1 - "Mumbai"
programmes.d: Pete Heat in Manchester and visits Old Trafford and for his finale; he wows a group of friends with his unique and comedic magic skills.
